summary: A standalone, easier-entry cooperative dungeon crawler that keeps Gloomhaven's card-driven combat and hand-management tension while trimming setup and rules overhead. You and up to three friends fight through a branching campaign of scenarios, retiring cards for stamina and racing the clock before your hand runs empty.
praised: much faster, friendlier onramp than base Gloomhaven
tense hand-management combat with meaningful initiative choices
criticised: still a real time investment with fiddly setup/teardown per scenario
limited character roster compared to full Gloomhaven
quarterbacking risk if one player reads all the rules

interaction.kind: cooperative turn-order combos and shared monster targeting on one battle map
interaction.detail: Because it's cooperative, players don't deny each other, but the shared initiative system, positioning on one map, and a common pool of monsters means every card and move is chosen around what teammates need — blocking a hex for an ally, timing a card to combo with theirs, or focusing the same enemy. Very little of the state is private; the map, monster health and turn order are all shared and constantly shaped by each player's choices.
interaction.said: "you have to combo initiative with your teammates", "one bad card ruins the whole round", "it's a puzzle you solve together"

subsystems: character leveling and personal battle goals
scoring.how_you_win: Players cooperatively complete the scenario's stated objective before any character is exhausted or the scenario's loss condition triggers; there is no competitive score, only scenario success or failure.

similar: Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avalon

theme.said: 'the card-based stamina system IS the fantasy of exhaustion,' praised for gloomy dungeon-crawl immersion rather than called pasted-on
theme.why: each character's hand doubles as both their available actions and their stamina bar, so a fighter tiring out mid-battle and being forced to long-rest is mechanically identical to running low on cards, directly modeling combat fatigue

style.why: Miniatures, a narrative campaign, and card/dice-resolved combat with character death drive the experience, far outweighing any economic optimization
